bugs.title: Shadow Clone creation silently stalls mid-copy — likely Worker execution timeout, resulting repo has only .clipforge-sync.json
bugs.notes: FIXED AND VERIFIED END-TO-END AGAINST THE LIVE GITHUB API. Root cause confirmed by direct code read: createPrivateShadowClone performed the entire bulk copy inside one Worker request (~300 files x 2 fully-awaited GitHub API calls each + tree/commit/PATCH), exceeding the Cloudflare Workers execution budget — the Worker was killed mid-loop after the self-contained bootstrap commit, exactly producing the 'only .clipforge-sync.json' symptom and the stuck 'Preparing repository...' progress. FIX: the bootstrap commit now also ships a one-time clone-copy.yml into the new repo (second Contents PUT on the bootstrap branch, alongside the sync marker); the Worker dispatches it (with retry on the new-workflow 404 indexing lag) and polls .clipforge-clone-status.json every 2s (start/stall/deadline watchdogs at 120s/360s/600s) — the same commit-a-status-file + bot-polls pattern as the job pipeline. The workflow copies the cloneable tree locally from a --filter=blob:none partial clone of the (public) source, pushes it as ONE fast-forward commit chain, and the bot then copies the source's own 8 workflow files + deletes the one-time workflow via the Contents API with the user's PAT. Three failure modes found and fixed ONLY through live end-to-end runs: (1) a bare 'while read' loop executes zero iterations under Actions' closed stdin (COPIED: 0 caught by the verify step) — file list now redirected via '<'; (2) pushes from GITHUB_TOKEN touching .github/workflows/* are remote-rejected AND Contents-API PUTs for workflow files are 403 — the push therefore contains no workflow paths and workflow files go through the bot's PAT (the same authority the original in-Worker copy used; onboarding already requires the workflow scope); (3) ~330 paced REST blob writes tripped GitHub's secondary rate limit (403 after minutes of retries) — eliminated by the single-push design. Also fixed: mawk cannot parse escaped slashes in awk regex constants (modes manifest uses substr/index instead); exec bits restored via chmod from an ls-tree modes manifest (the source ships one 100755 script); printf '\n' inside the JS template literal must be written '\\n' or the emitted YAML breaks. bug-46 bootstrap-first + bug-47 default-branch normalization logic preserved untouched; post-conditions still verify the default branch head and blob count against the live API (floor adjusted: the workflow push verifies >= TOTAL-WFCOUNT server-side, the bot verifies >= TOTAL after the PAT workflow writes land). Live verification: fresh repo clipforge-test-bug63-0iluoi created by the real createPrivateShadowClone() — 303 blobs on main (302 source files incl. all 8 workflows + sync marker), one-time workflow removed, bot/src/github.js byte-identical to the source blob, live progress streamed (copy 50..294/294, finalize), ~63s total, test repo deleted (404 confirmed). Bot test suite 110/110 pass. (Note: commit sha is 72e79e9 after rebasing onto the concurrent cleanup commit fb5c233.)

bugs.title: Series Part 2 Stage A still failing — 'release not found' during evidence reuse
bugs.notes: FIXED. Investigation confirmed the reuse step NOW triggers (bug-61's gating fix landed and works) but dies with 'release not found' because of WHICH release it targets. Root cause: bug-61's fix rests on a false premise — its comments assert 'series id == Part 1's job id', but wizard.js assigns the job id as manual-<Date.now()> (line 39) while index.js assigns series_id as series-<Date.now()> (lines 446/562, a DIFFERENT timestamp). bug-61 seeded Part 1's source_job_id with the series id (wizard.js:172) and series.js:152's fallback also used series_id, so every part >= 2 inherited a series id as its source_job_id and stage-a's reuse step ran `gh release download clipforge-series-<ts>` — a release that NEVER exists (Part 1's Stage B publishes clipforge-<job_id> = clipforge-manual-<ts>). That is exactly the screenshot's 'release not found'. The prompt's hypothesis (2) was right in shape (wrong id used) but the specific wrong id is the series id, not the part's own job id. FIX, three layers: (1) wizard.js — Part 1's source_job_id is now wizard.jobId (the id its release is published under); covers both creation paths since the telegram_relay path also routes through wizardToRequest. (2) series.js + index.js — nextPartRequestBody gained a 4th param currentJobId and its legacy fallback (blank source_job_id in a pre-fix Part 1 request) now resolves to the COMPLETING part's own job id, passed from startNextSeriesPart where the job has just reached 'complete' so its release provably exists — never the series_id. (3) stage-a.yml — the 'Resolve job + read the Stage A request' reader re-points any 'series-'-shaped source_job_id at the current job's Part 1 (<series_id>-p1) at read time (job ids for a Part >= 2 continuation never start with 'series-', so the rewrite cannot misfire), which repairs bug-61-era requests like the failing series-1787915980098-p2 WITHOUT needing the deployed bot to update first; the gh release download also retries 6x at 15s intervals so a continuation queued immediately after Part 1 completes cannot die on release-propagation lag (the prompt's hypothesis 3, a minor residual risk — Stage B's release upload precedes its status write, so the window is tiny). VALIDATED: bot suite 110/110; the reader's embedded Python was executed against three fixtures — legacy series-id shape repaired to series-1787915980098-p1, blank stays blank, valid manual-555 untouched; the reuse step's bash passes bash -n; stage-a.yml parses as valid YAML; the series fallback test was rewritten to the corrected expectation. NOT fully end-to-end live-tested (would require running a real 2-part series through the pipeline — the deployed bot must be redeployed for layer 1/2 to take effect, while layer 3 repairs existing bad requests on any runner).

bugs.title: Remove manual 'push update to clones' trigger — updates to clones must be fully automatic
bugs.notes: Design reversal: remove manual 'Push update to clones' button from Settings; on every push to main on the main account, automatically propagate the update to all connected clones reusing the existing sync/copy logic; preserve the changelog/notification-to-clone-owner behavior; preserve owner-identity gating (main vs clone) for source-of-truth determination.
